findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:549-550 hardcodes the literal string proof-or-stop for the bin key lookup instead of reusing the existing CANONICAL_ROOT_PACKAGE_NAME constant (defined at line 117 and already used at lines 1153/1291 for the same command name). Low risk of drift if the bin/command name is ever renamed in one place but not the other.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 8fcf66f31e: the bin-key lookup in packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts now uses bin[CANONICAL_ROOT_PACKAGE_NAME] on both the guard and the read instead of the literal string; tsc lint green.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:558-561,613-616 (inspectGlobalCoreExecutable + checkGlobalCoreRealpath) added in this story a distinct warning branch for a global bin target that is missing/not-a-file (executableFacts.binTargetExists=false), which renders a different remediation string ("...does not exist; rebuild: npm --prefix <realpath> run build") than the non-executable-mode branch. CHK-003:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence (packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs cases 4 and 5) only exercises: case 4 = bin target present but mode 0644 (non-executable, file exists), case 5 = .worktrees/ realpath drift with an executable bin. Neither case, nor any other verificationEvidence for CHK-003, constructs a package whose declared bin target file is absent or is a directory, so the ENOENT/non-file sub-branch and its rebuild remediation string are never executed by any test -- grep for rebuild|does not exist across the test file returns zero hits. This is exactly the kind of drift the story is meant to catch (a broken/missing build artifact behind global proof-or-stop), so the untested branch is in-scope, not incidental.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 8fcf66f31e adds fixture cases 7 gcr-absent-bin-warn (ENOENT, binMode null) and 8 gcr-dir-bin-warn (directory) to packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs, each asserting the exact 'global bin target <abs> does not exist; rebuild: npm --prefix <realpath> run build' warning and no chmod/drift text; node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs -> ok global-core-realpath.

findings.desc: commit b13839b411 (git cherry-pick -x from story/B-83aa 8ebfff3550) modifies packages/main/src/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts and packages/main/src/tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts, neither of which is in .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/scope-contract.json allowedModify/allowedCreate, and no checklist item carries a reason for the scope change. Content verified correct (byte-identical body to 8ebfff3550, cwd-neutrality assertion is non-vacuous, DYNAMIC_BINDING_BUILD_CEILING 808->809 is harmless since B-e256 adds no new .ts source and the guard still reports builds=808), but the story now carries an unreviewed-under-this-story, cross-story commit authored for B-83aa CHK-004 embedded via cherry-pick before B-83aa has landed on main. This is a scope-contract/provenance gap (mode=shadow, so not mechanically blocked), not a functional defect: recommend amending scope-contract/checklist to record the reason, or landing the shared F-023/ceiling fixture fix on main directly instead of duplicating it across in-flight stories via cherry-pick.
findings.resolvedReason: Scope contract widened with an explicit scopeChangeReason naming commit b13839b411 (cherry-pick -x of B-83aa 8ebfff3550), why the fixture repair is needed for this story's own validate (CHK-002 registers a validate command, which moved the pinned F-023 digest) and why the identical commit was taken (no merge conflict at B-83aa DONE); both fixture files are now in allowedModify/allowedTest. The reviewer's broader point (land shared fixture repairs once on main instead of per-story cherry-picks) is accepted: B-83aa carries the canonical commit and merges first.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1576-1587 defaultCompiledCoreVersionProbe (the production probe actually wired by default at line 248) has two branches -- the readFileSync catch (unbuilt/missing dist/core/proof-or-stop-brand.js, ENOENT) and the COMPILED_CORE_VERSION_RE non-match (partially built or unparsable content) -- that are never exercised by any test using the DEFAULT probe. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs case 29 (around lines 950-970) only injects a compiledCoreVersionProbe STUB via extraOptions to simulate a probe failure; writeCorePackage/makeRepoWithWorktree never pass compiledVersion:null (which would skip writing the brand file) or malformed brand-file content, so the real function's own ENOENT and unparsable-content error messages are dead-in-tests. Separately, unlike its sibling BRAND_EXPORT_RE in core/version-bump.ts (which the doc comment at lines 1562-1573 claims this is the same regex shape as), this probe applies COMPILED_CORE_VERSION_RE with no comment-stripping and no duplicate/ambiguous-match guard -- version-bump.ts throws on more than one match (version-bump.ts:213-218) precisely because a second export-shaped occurrence (e.g. in a comment) would let exec() silently pick the wrong one; defaultCompiledCoreVersionProbe has no equivalent check, so a future brand-file comment change that happens to contain export-shaped text would silently report the wrong compiled version rather than failing loudly. Low risk today (no such occurrence exists in the real file) but it is exactly the untested/unguarded shape this round was asked to scrutinize.

packages/main/src/core/version-bump.ts:210 (commit 47382c6681) is modified (export added to findBrandExport) outside the story scope-contract allowedModify list (scope_contract_check reports OUT_OF_SCOPE warn, mode=shadow) and there is no scope_question_resolve / acknowledgement recorded anywhere in the story artifacts (scope-contract.json, checklist.json, scope-check.json) naming this file. The change itself is small and sound (adds an `export` keyword plus a doc comment, no behavior change to version-bump.ts, verified byte-identical logic via mutation test), but it is an unacknowledged scope expansion that the CLAUDE.md scope-contract process requires to be declared/acknowledged rather than silently landed.
findings.resolvedReason: packages/main/src/core/version-bump.ts is now acknowledged in the scope contract with the reason the reviewer asked for: F-004 required the probe to share the existing ambiguity guard, so findBrandExport was exported, a one-keyword change with no behaviour change. The reviewer verified the direction is leaf utility to consumer with no import cycle. scope_contract_check no longer reports it unacknowledged.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1932 renders version from actual.version (package.json) even though the new compiled-runtime probe stores the executable’s authoritative version in actual.compiledVersion. When package.json is 2.0.0 but dist still serves 1.9.0, the global-core-realpath summary row therefore says version=2.0.0 while its warning says the compiled runtime reports 1.9.0; this contradicts the promised reported-version diagnostic and can mislead operators. Render compiledVersion (or clearly label both manifest and compiled values) and add a stale-compiled-version row assertion. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 renders the authoritative compiledVersion in the global CLI row, with stale-manifest regression assertions in global-core-realpath.test.mjs.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:52 fixed-clock waitForFile deletion is incomplete: DESCENDANT_PID_READY_TIMEOUT_MS remains as an unused declaration after every consumer was replaced by lifecycle-bounded waitForChildFile; this dead residue contradicts the new child-lifecycle waiting concept and can mislead future maintenance. severity=critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 removes the unused DESCENDANT_PID_READY_TIMEOUT_MS residue; repository search confirms the deleted symbol and stale guidance references are absent.

findings.desc: quality-runtime-probe-parse: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1566-1568 accepts every non-empty `npm root -g` stdout value as a valid filesystem root, although the new structured-probe contract says unparsable output must be a failure. Verified against the built candidate with PATH resolving `npm` to `/bin/echo`: stdout `root -g` produced globalCoreRealpath.status=pass, installed=false, and npmRoot=`root -g`. A noisy, wrapped, or corrupt npm response is therefore misreported as known absence and defeats the fail-closed doctor diagnostic. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 rejects multiline or non-absolute npm root output as a structured probe failure; the production-path fake npm regression passes.

findings.desc: quality-bin-target-stat-probe: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-708 catches every statSync failure and reports binTargetExists=false with verification=ok. Verified against the built frozen candidate using an existing executable bin below a mode-000 parent: stat failed with EACCES, but globalCoreRealpath said the target does not exist and prescribed only npm rebuild. This conflates an unreadable or I/O-failed installed target with ENOENT, discards the errno, and can send operators through a rebuild that cannot repair permissions or filesystem access. Preserve non-ENOENT probe failures as unverifiable drift with the errno and add a hermetic denied-stat case. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 preserves non-ENOENT stat failures as bin-target-stat-failed with errno and unknown existence/executable facts; the hermetic EACCES regression passes.

findings.desc: quality-bin-target-containment-prefix: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:98-100 treats every relative path beginning with `..` as outside `dist`. A valid package.json bin target such as `dist/..cli.js` yields `relative(...) === "..cli.js"`, so restoreBinExecutableBits skips it; a targeted probe against the frozen candidate returned restored=[] and left mode 0644. This violates the CHK-001 contract to restore every listed in-dist bin target and can leave the linked CLI non-executable. Use an exact parent traversal check and add a hermetic in-dist dot-prefix case. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 uses an exact parent-traversal predicate, so dist/..cli.js is restored; the dot-prefixed target regression passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:139,160,203,230,258 only exercise a one-entry object-form package.json bin, while scripts/promote-dist.mjs:93-96 contains a distinct string-shorthand branch and iterates arbitrary object values. Repository search found no test using bin:"dist/cli.js" or two declared bin targets. A regression could leave a shorthand target or one of multiple targets at 0644 while every current selector remains GREEN, contradicting CHK-001 and the plan promise to restore every listed package.json bin target. Add hermetic string-shorthand and multi-target cases that assert every target becomes executable, remains byte-identical, and appears in the restored list. This is distinct from F-010, which covers the in-dist containment prefix boundary. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 covers package.json bin string shorthand and multiple targets, asserting every target is executable, byte-identical, and listed.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/validation-tier-planner-smoke.ts:469,483 deletes the PIN MAINTENANCE guidance block but leaves two live references to the now-nonexistent maintenance note ("the maintenance note above" and "see PIN MAINTENANCE above"). Repository-wide rg confirms no PIN MAINTENANCE block remains, so future validate.commands digest drift points maintainers to instructions that this Story removed; the deletion is incomplete and the residual assertion/comment are misleading. severity=critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 removes both dangling PIN MAINTENANCE references and replaces them with self-contained digest maintenance guidance.

findings.desc: quality-bin-target-type-validation: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:101-103 chmods and records every lexically in-dist target without verifying that statSync(target).isFile(). A targeted frozen-candidate probe declared dist/cli.js as a directory: restoreBinExecutableBits returned ["dist/cli.js"], changed its mode to 0755, and the target remained a directory. promoteDist therefore accepts and promotes a malformed staging tree while reporting the bin target restored even though the global CLI target is not an executable file. packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs covers absent targets and stat/chmod failures but has no non-regular-target case. Reject non-regular bin targets before promotion and add a hermetic directory case. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 uses lstat and rejects non-regular bin targets before promotion; the directory fixture proves old dist remains untouched.

findings.desc: quality-smoke-descendant-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:312-338 and 405-425 kill only the direct CLI child on the harness ceiling or wait bound, then fail without cleaning the command descendants; the alive-descendant assertion also has no cleanup when it detects the regression. A bounded process-tree probe matching this parent-only SIGKILL behavior verified that the parent closed while its sleep descendant remained alive. Because descendantTreeCommand launches sleep 600 for the command, idle, and max rows, the exact failure paths this smoke is meant to diagnose can leave orphan processes running for up to ten minutes and contaminate later validation. Retain a process-group or descendant cleanup handle and terminate/reap it in a finally path before failing. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 adds process-tree cleanup and reaping to startCli plus finally cleanup of published descendant PIDs; validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke passes.

findings.desc: quality-smoke-platform-regression: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts:352-357 hard-codes /bin/sh and the external sleep utility for every new descendantTreeCommand row, replacing the prior process.execPath-based child fixture. proof-or-stop.config.json registers this smoke as an unconditional validation command, while the validation implementation and validation-tier planner explicitly model native win32 execution. On native Windows, spawning /bin/sh fails with ENOENT before the descendant PID can be published, so the command, idle, and max deadline assertions cannot exercise their subject and escalated/full validation fails for host reasons. Use process.execPath with a platform-neutral inline descendant fixture, or provide an explicit win32 branch with equivalent process-tree semantics. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 replaces the /bin/sh sleep fixture with process.execPath and Node built-ins; validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke passes.

findings.desc: quality-bin-target-symlink-escape: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:101-103 validates only the lexical bin path, then statSync/chmodSync follow an in-tree symlink. A targeted probe against the frozen candidate created dist/cli.js as a symlink to an outside 0644 file; restoreBinExecutableBits returned ["dist/cli.js"] and changed the outside file to 0755. This lets a malformed or compromised staging tree mutate permissions outside the promoted tree while falsely reporting the bin restored. It is distinct from F-010 (the lexical `..` prefix boundary) and F-013 (a directory/non-regular target): statSync(target).isFile() would still accept this symlink because its referent is a file. Reject symlink targets or verify the resolved target remains inside the promoted tree, and add a hermetic symlink-escape case. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 721bb624b0 uses lstat to reject symlink bin targets before chmod; the escape fixture proves the outside referent stays mode 0644.

findings.desc: quality-bin-target-intermediate-symlink-escape: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:98-110 checks lexical containment and lstatSyncs only the final path component, so an in-tree intermediate directory symlink is followed. A current-HEAD bounded probe declared bin dist/linked/cli.js where dist/linked symlinked to an outside directory; restoreBinExecutableBits returned ["dist/linked/cli.js"] and changed the outside referent from 0644 to 0755. F-016 is therefore only partially resolved: rejecting a final-component symlink does not prevent nested symlink traversal. Resolve/realpath the target and verify it remains under the real promoted tree, or reject any symlink component, and add the hermetic intermediate-symlink escape case. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 528a0ebcb resolves both tree and target realpaths and refuses any target whose resolved path leaves the real promoted staging tree before chmod. Hermetic c6 proves an intermediate directory symlink cannot change the outside referent and leaves the old dist intact.

findings.desc: quality-global-row-version-fallback: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1958-1962 fixes F-006 only when compiledVersion is known; when the compiled-runtime probe fails, the nullish fallback silently renders the package.json manifest as the generic version= value. Existing missing/unreadable/malformed compiled-artifact cases set compiledVersion=null but do not assert the row, so a manifest at 2.0.0 with an absent or unparsable dist artifact still renders version=2.0.0 while warnings say the compiled runtime is unverifiable. That generic row value is not the executable’s authoritative version and remains misleading. Render version=unknown for a failed compiled probe, or label manifestVersion and compiledVersion separately, and cover the existing probe-failure/default-probe cases. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 528a0ebcb renders the compact global-core row from compiledVersion only, falling back to version=unknown rather than package manifest version. global-core-realpath probe-failure cases assert unknown and reject version=0.0.0 fallback.

findings.desc: quality-symlink-regression-portability: packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:248-259 unconditionally calls symlinkSync in a validation command registered for every host. Native Windows can reject file-symlink creation with EPERM when the account lacks Create Symbolic Links privilege or Developer Mode, so this F-016 regression case can fail before exercising restoreBinExecutableBits even though the implementation may be correct. This reintroduces a host-dependent failure alongside the F-015 portability repair. Use a privilege-independent directory junction/intermediate-link fixture where equivalent, or explicitly feature-probe and report/skip only the unsupported symlink construction while retaining safety coverage on capable hosts. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 528a0ebcb wraps symlink fixtures in an explicit Windows capability probe that skips only EPERM, EACCES, or ENOSYS; all other construction failures remain test failures, while capable hosts retain both final and intermediate symlink safety coverage.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:248-260 covers F-016 only when the final bin path component is a symlink. It has no case where an intermediate directory component is a symlink. At current HEAD, a bounded temp-dir probe declared bin dist/linked/cli.js with dist/linked symlinked to an outside directory; scripts/promote-dist.mjs:98-110 returned ["dist/linked/cli.js"] and changed the outside file from 0644 to 0755. Thus the committed F-016 regression is under-broad and does not detect the live intermediate-symlink escape independently recorded as B-e256:F-017. Add a hermetic intermediate-component symlink case that proves the outside referent stays 0644 and restoration fails before promotion. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 528a0ebcb adds hermetic c6, which promotes a staging tree containing an intermediate directory symlink and asserts EINVAL, unchanged outside mode 0644, untouched old dist, retained staging, and no trash.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: commit 3b2f136af6 replaced post-promotion chmod with restoreBinExecutableBits(staging, dist) before the old dist is evicted (scripts/promote-dist.mjs:16-22), so a chmod failure preserves the working dist. The authoritative Story inputs still carry the deleted model: plan.md:13 requires restoreBinExecutableBits(dist) after rmSync(trash), checklist.json:6 says chmod after renaming staging into dist, understanding.json:7 describes the GREEN candidate as after promotion, and summary.json:3 says the helper runs after every dist promotion. This is not F-017/F-020 symlink containment or coverage: it is a separate incomplete concept replacement that makes the final delivery summary and review context contradict the implemented crash-safety invariant. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Story truth was legally reopened and corrected through CLI lifecycle: commit 528a0ebcb updates plan.md; checklist context, Story description, scope boundary, background, understanding, and summary now consistently require staging validation and chmod before old-dist eviction. Both INIT reviewers passed with zero issues and the current scope-plan reviewer saved zero-gap evidence.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:27-29 and :96 retain the live DESIRED-property/assertion wording that the pipeline restores bin executable bits after promotion. The current implementation and corrected Story contract call restoreBinExecutableBits(staging, dist) before evicting the old dist; these are active expectation/selector statements, not the historical pre-fix narrative, so they preserve the deleted post-promotion model and can mislead future maintenance. Severity: critical.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 26418e0846 labels the pre-fix mechanism Historical RED and rewrites the active DESIRED property plus pipeline assertion to require staging validation and restoration before renameSync(dist, trash). The focused red test reports that staging restoration precedes old-dist eviction and passes.

findings.desc: quality-win32-executable-mode-contract: packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:77-86 and 150-166 unconditionally require POSIX 0o111 mode bits before and after chmod, while the only Windows adaptation at lines 134-147 skips unsupported symlink construction. On Windows, Node chmod does not provide a meaningful POSIX execute-bit contract and npm executes package bins through generated .cmd shims, so this newly registered validation command can fail even when the global CLI works. Platform-gate the POSIX mode assertions or define and test the Windows shim contract; the current symlink-capability skip does not cover this core portability failure. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 26418e0846 makes the regression platform-aware: POSIX retains 0o111 assertions; Windows validates the shebang or npm command-shim target, byte content, promotion cleanup, and c4/c6 pre-eviction safety. Only unavailable POSIX chmod-denial injections d/f are skipped there with an explicit named reason.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:25-30 still defines CHK-001:happy:0 as a universal must intent that a 0644 target gains POSIX 0o111 bits and pins the POSIX-only GREEN label, while packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:83-85 and :178-182 explicitly replace that assertion and label on win32 with an npm-shim-target content contract. .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/proofstory.json:43-49 also binds that stale intent and universally claims 0644 becomes 0755 after promotion. F-022 staging-before-eviction wording is corrected, but the F-023 portability repair did not reach the machine-owned Story acceptance contract: on win32 the must selector cannot appear even when the test passes. Repair the verification intent and ProofStory acceptance binding so POSIX mode restoration and Windows shim-target behavior are expressed without a contradictory universal 0o111/0755 promise. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 1e1e346043 and CLI-owned contract commits c0a6148, 6868d4f, and 639594b replace the universal POSIX 0644-to-0755 promise with a platform-correct POSIX executable-bit versus Windows npm-shim contract. CHK-001 now pins contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored; verification refresh passed and current full validation passed all 132 commands.

findings.desc: quality-win32-pinned-selector-portability: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:30 pins CHK-001:happy:0 to the POSIX-only GREEN label, while packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:179-182 deliberately emits a different Windows label after the F-023 repair. A read-only simulated win32 branch run exited 0 but selectorMatched=false, so a Windows verification-evidence refresh would reject a correct passing run even though the registered full validation now succeeds. Use a platform-invariant selector/output line or a platform-aware supported evidence contract. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of F-024's narrower selector facet. CHK-001 now pins the platform-invariant contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored marker emitted by both supported platform branches; the refreshed mechanical receipt matched it and the full 132-command validation passed.

findings.desc: test-coverage-win32-global-core-contract: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:365-381 pins three CHK-003 must intents to `node packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs`, but packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:107-110 unconditionally creates a directory symlink with no Windows capability probe and :201-217 universally requires a 0644 target to be non-executable with a `chmod +x` remediation. Production packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:667-672 explicitly short-circuits the executable access probe to true on win32 because Windows has no POSIX execute-bit contract. Read-only probes verified both failure paths: with simulated win32 and symlink support the test exits 1 at line 211 because status is pass, and with simulated EPERM symlink denial it terminates at line 110. Therefore `ok global-core-realpath` is unreachable on affected Windows hosts and no evidence covers the Windows npm .cmd/shim doctor contract. This is distinct from F-024/F-025, which cover CHK-001 and red-global-cli-exec-bit. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 1e1e346043 adds symlink-capability probes and a Windows X_OK/npm-shim branch to global-core-realpath.test.mjs, while retaining POSIX chmod semantics only on POSIX. CHK-003 was updated to the platform-correct contract and the focused suite plus full 132-command validation passed.

findings.desc: test-coverage-host-bound-doctor-selector: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:343-351 defines CHK-003:happy:0 as a must intent but pins its doctor selector to the submitter-specific macOS absolute path `global-core-realpath [hard] /Users/jek/Documents/GitHub/Prooforstop/packages/main version=`. The stored receipt at checklist.json:470-485 proves only that checkout and cannot be refreshed in a Windows checkout (or any clone at another root) even when doctor emits a correct global-core-realpath row. Use a path-invariant selector plus fixture assertions for the resolved root, or a supported platform-aware selector contract. This is distinct from F-025, which concerns CHK-001's POSIX-only hermetic label. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: CLI-owned checklist commit 6868d4f changes CHK-003 happy evidence from the submitter-specific absolute path to contract: global-core-realpath-pass. The current doctor receipt matched this host-independent marker and the full 132-command validation passed.

findings.desc: quality-win32-remediation-command: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:558-560 implements only POSIX single-quote escaping, and :681-682 uses it to emit `cd -- <root> && npm link`; the new global-core drift branches also emit `ls -ld` at :847, :879, and :933. On native Windows every drive path contains backslashes, so shellQuote wraps it in literal single quotes, while cmd.exe neither treats single quotes as quoting nor accepts `cd --`; `ls -ld` is also unavailable by default. Thus the Story's promised exact one-line doctor remediation is not executable on Windows even after the F-026 test-coverage gap is fixed. This is a production-output quality defect distinct from F-024/F-025 selectors and F-026/F-027 evidence portability. Render a platform-valid remediation (for example an argv-equivalent npm --prefix form with platform quoting) and cover it. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 1e1e346043 renders Windows remediation with cmd.exe-valid cd /d and double-quoted paths, replaces POSIX-only ls syntax with a Windows dir form, and covers the exact output in global-core-realpath.test.mjs. Focused and full 132-command validation passed.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:376 and proofstory.json:49 now promise that the Windows branch validates the npm command-shim contract, but packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:693-695 returns true for every win32 bin target solely from the platform value, while inspectGlobalCoreExecutable at :737-769 only stats the declared dist/cli.js file and never locates, reads, or validates a generated proof-or-stop.cmd/.ps1 shim. The alleged Windows regression at packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:1229-1240 likewise creates no command shim; it merely injects platform=win32 and asserts that the unconditional true is returned. A missing, stale, or malformed global Windows shim can therefore coexist with executable=yes and the global-core-realpath PASS marker. F-026's resolution claim is not delivered: either validate the actual shim/target relationship or narrow the Story contract and finding resolution to the Node-target-only fact. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit d65767d4b16e validates the PATH-selected Windows npm command shim against the declared canonical bin target; CHK-003 happy:1 and adversarial:2 execute the representative valid, missing, unreadable, and mismatched shim cases. Full current-material validate passed 132/132.

findings.desc: quality-win32-command-path-percent-expansion: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-707 states that wrapping a Windows path in double quotes is sufficient for cmd.exe metacharacters, and the F-028 resolution relies on this helper for cd /d, npm --prefix, and dir remediation. That is false for the legal Windows filename character `%`: cmd.exe expands `%NAME%` even inside double quotes, so a canonical checkout such as C:\\work\\%TEMP%\\Prooforstop is rewritten to the environment variable value and every emitted remediation targets the wrong path. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:172-184 mirrors the same incomplete quoting and its Windows case uses only a space-containing POSIX temp path, so it cannot catch percent expansion. F-028 is therefore not fully resolved for valid Windows paths; render an actually literal cmd.exe path representation or constrain/report unsupported paths, with a regression containing paired percent signs. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Commit d65767d4b16e replaces cmd.exe double-quoted remediation with a UTF-16LE PowerShell EncodedCommand using Set-Location -LiteralPath; the regression includes spaces, apostrophes, and paired percent tokens and passes in CHK-003 adversarial:0.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:10 still states as an unqualified user-visible result that `ls -la packages/main/dist/cli.js` shows `-rwxr-xr-x` after a rebuild. That contradicts the repaired cross-platform intent at checklist.json:25 and ProofStory AC-001 at proofstory.json:49, which correctly use POSIX executable bits versus a byte-identical Windows npm-shim target. delivery-check.json:11-14 repeats the universal promise and marks it delivered only with POSIX `ls -la`/0755 evidence. On Windows neither `ls -la` nor `-rwxr-xr-x` is the observable contract, so the machine-owned F-024 cross-platform acceptance family remains partially unresolved despite the repaired intent/selector. Repair CHK-001.userSees and refresh its dependent delivery evidence through the CLI. severity: critical

quality-win32-cmd-percent-expansion: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:703-707 claims that wrapping a Windows path in double quotes is sufficient for cmd.exe and leaves the path bytes unchanged. cmd.exe expands `%VariableName%` tokens on command lines, including quoted arguments, while `%` is legal in Windows file and directory names. A valid canonical root such as `C:\repo\%TEMP%\core` is therefore rendered at :710-717 as `cd /d "C:\repo\%TEMP%\core" && npm link` or an equivalent `npm --prefix` command and targets the environment-expanded path instead of the literal checkout. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:1229-1279 covers spaces but no percent-delimited component, so its simulated win32 assertions cannot catch this. F-028 exact cmd.exe remediation is therefore not fully closed. Render a command that preserves literal percent characters for the intended cmd.exe usage and add a percent-path fixture. severity: medium
findings.resolvedReason: Duplicate of F-030. The same d65767d4b16e encoded PowerShell LiteralPath remediation and percent-token regression closes both observations.

findings.desc: test-coverage-win32-capability-skip-false-pass: packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:83-87 handles an unavailable Windows directory-link capability by printing `ok global-core-realpath` and exiting 0 before any of cases 1-34 run. All three CHK-003 must intents pin exactly that selector, so on an EPERM/EACCES/ENOSYS Windows host the CLI can issue passing mechanical receipts for canonical/drift/non-git, platform executable semantics, and adversarial remediation while executing zero assertions—including the supposedly every-host win32 case 34 at :1224-1284. This is a distinct evidence-integrity gap beyond F-029 (no real shim validation) and F-030 (cmd percent quoting): the F-026 portability repair changed a setup failure into an indistinguishable green result. Limit the skip to link-dependent cases or introduce a fixture seam for the platform-only assertions, and ensure skipped execution cannot match the acceptance selector. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit d65767d4b16e limits capability skips to link-dependent cases and adds assertion-count guards so zero assertions cannot print the pinned ok selector; CHK-003 edge:2 and full validate pass.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:737-769 and :951-1128 verify the canonical package root but only stat/access the lexical package.json bin target. statSync follows a symlink, and the target realpath is never resolved or checked against the canonical package. A current built-candidate temporary probe made canonical-core/dist/cli.js a symlink to an executable under .worktrees/stale/dist/cli.js; globalCoreRealpath still returned status=pass, executable=true, remediation=null, and rendered contract: global-core-realpath-pass. Thus CHK-003 and the Story background promise to diagnose the global executable realpath can false-pass when the package root is canonical but the actual POSIX bin target escapes to an ephemeral worktree. F-029 is Windows npm-shim validation; this is a distinct POSIX bin-target-realpath chain. Resolve and validate the bin target realpath/containment and add a regression. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit d65767d4b16e resolves the final bin target realpath, rejects final and intermediate symlink escapes outside the canonical package, and preserves realpath errno diagnostics; CHK-003 adversarial:1 passes.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/checklist.json:356-361 promises that when no global proof-or-stop is on PATH the global-core row is informational and names how to link one, but packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:772-950 never consults context.cliEntrypoint and instead classifies presence only from npm root -g plus the package entry. The purported edge regression at packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:159-169 and :310-349 injects a fake commandResolver while merely emptying the npm global root, so it does not exercise the promised no-PATH premise. A current built-candidate temporary probe with commandResolver=()=>null and a healthy canonical package under the global npm root produced cli-entrypoint=warn but global-core-realpath=pass, remediation=null, and the resolved-install contract marker instead of the promised informational link guidance. This is a distinct PATH-vs-global-package presence contract gap, not F-029 shim validation or F-031 platform wording. Align the intent with package-presence semantics or make the global-core row consume PATH presence, and test the actual premise. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit d65767d4b16e makes a missing PATH-selected proof-or-stop command non-pass with relink remediation even when the package exists; CHK-003 edge:1 exercises the actual premise and full validate passes.

findings.desc: promotion-manifest-read-error-false-success: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:87-91 catches every package.json read/parse error and returns [], so promoteDist at :16-35 continues to evict the working dist even when the manifest probe observed EACCES/EPERM/EIO rather than a benign missing or malformed manifest. A current built-candidate temporary probe chmodded package.json to 000, kept old dist/cli.js at 0755 and staging at 0644, then called promoteDist; it returned without throwing, replaced the old CLI with the new body, and left the promoted target mode 0644 (observed {threw:null,body:"new\n",mode:"644"}). This defeats the primary background/checklist promise to validate/restore declared staging bin targets before eviction and conflicts with understanding.json's only-ENOENT-benign constraint; the pinned adversarial evidence tests only missing and syntactically unparseable manifests, not a non-absence read failure. Preserve non-absence manifest read errors and abort before eviction, or explicitly reconcile the conflicting acceptance contract and prove the chosen failure behavior. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit d65767d4b16e treats only missing or malformed manifest data as the documented benign no-bin cases; injected EACCES/EPERM/EIO-style non-absence reads propagate before old-dist eviction. CHK-001 adversarial:1 and the GREEN hermetic c1 selector pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:761-767 and packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:247-258: CHK-003 adversarial shim coverage remains falsifiable because validateWindowsCommandShim treats any non-comment line containing the expected target plus node, exec, or _prog as an invocation. A current-head probe used an echo line naming the correct target followed by a node command invoking another target; global-core-realpath still returned pass with verification=ok, executable=true, remediation=null, and the contract marker. The existing mismatch test puts the expected target only in an @REM line, so it cannot catch a non-comment but non-executing reference. This is distinct from resolved F-029, where Windows validation passed without inspecting a shim: inspection now runs, but its invocation heuristic false-accepts a broken shim. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 restricts Windows shim acceptance to actual invoking command segments and rejects echo, REM, SET, GOTO, and other non-executing decoys. The cross-platform global-core fixture and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1049-1096 rejects an absent PATH command, but inspectGlobalCoreExecutable at :861-867 validates the PATH-selected shim only on Windows; the POSIX branch checks X_OK on the canonical package bin target without verifying that a present PATH executable resolves to that target. renderRuntimeEnvironmentReport at :318-328 can therefore emit contract: global-core-realpath-pass while cli-entrypoint is fail. Reproduction against the current built runtime with platform=linux, commandResolver returning an executable bogus temp proof-or-stop path, the real npm root -g, and executableAccessProbe=true produced cli-entrypoint=fail, global-core-realpath=pass, marker=true. This directly falsifies ProofStory AC-001 and summary.json:3-7, which promise that the healthy marker requires PATH/package/bin-target agreement. Add POSIX PATH-command realpath agreement to the global-core fact and a wrong-but-present PATH regression. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 requires the POSIX PATH-selected proof-or-stop command realpath to equal the declared canonical package bin target before emitting global-core-realpath-pass. The wrong-PATH healthy-package regression and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: quality-windows-path-command-selection: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1718-1747 prepends the extensionless proof-or-stop file before every PATHEXT candidate and treats any regular file as runnable on win32. Windows resolves an unqualified command through executable extensions, so in an npm-style bin directory containing the extensionless shell shim beside proof-or-stop.cmd, doctor can inspect the wrong file rather than the command the host actually launches. A current built-runtime probe set process.platform=win32 and PATHEXT=.COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD, placed a valid extensionless shim beside a broken proof-or-stop.cmd, and used the production resolver: cliEntrypoint selected the extensionless file, global-core-realpath returned pass/verification=ok, and the contract marker was emitted. This is distinct from F-037: even a perfect content parser still validates the wrong PATH artifact. Model Windows command lookup using PATHEXT order and add a production-resolver regression with competing bare and .cmd shims. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 resolves Windows commands in actual PATHEXT order without preferring an extensionless file. The hermetic ordering regression and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: promotion-missing-target-symlink-escape: scripts/promote-dist.mjs:117-138 performs lstat on the final staging bin path before resolving containment and treats every ENOENT as a benign absent target. If an intermediate staging directory is already a symlink outside the promoted tree but the outside final filename does not exist, lstat throws ENOENT before the realpath containment check. A current-head temporary probe built dist/linked -> outside with no outside/cli.js and package bin dist/linked/cli.js; restoreBinExecutableBits returned [] without throwing, so promoteDist would proceed to evict the working dist and promote the escaped, broken tree. The existing c6 regression only creates an existing outside referent and therefore reaches realpath. This violates background.md/plan.md and CHK-001, which require intermediate symlink escapes to be rejected before eviction and reserve benign handling for genuinely absent targets. Validate containment of the resolvable parent chain before classifying final ENOENT, and add an absent-referent escape regression. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 checks existing parent-chain containment before treating a missing final bin target as benign, so an intermediate symlink escape with an absent outside target aborts promotion. red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs case c7 and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: CHK-003:adversarial:2 has no executable coverage for its promised unreadable Windows npm command-shim branch. packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:742-752 classifies commandShimReadProbe failures as windows-command-shim-missing or windows-command-shim-unreadable, but packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:229-302 covers only a target-mismatched shim and an ENOENT missing shim. Repository search finds no commandShimReadProbe injection and no assertion for windows-command-shim-unreadable; the EIO fixture at lines 261-276 instead injects binTargetStatProbe and exercises the unrelated bin-target-stat-failed branch. checklist.json:645 nevertheless claims the receipt covered missing, unreadable, and mismatched shims. Thus the unreadable branch can regress while the pinned ok global-core-realpath selector remains green. This is distinct from F-037, which is a parser false-positive after a shim was read, and from resolved F-029, which concerned unconditional validation. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 adds an injected commandShimReadProbe failure exercising windows-command-shim-unreadable and asserts the healthy marker is suppressed. global-core-realpath.test.mjs and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1957-1977 collapses a failed or empty `git worktree list --porcelain` canonical-main probe into the current self-project's local packages/main path. Then :1097-1110 only warns that the resolved global package is inside `.worktrees` when `pathMatches` is already false. A current-built-runtime probe ran from the B-e256 worktree with PATH set to a directory containing no git, a temporary global @proof-or-stop/core symlink to that same Story worktree, and the matching worktree CLI; it produced expected=<B-e256>/packages/main, worktreeCheckout=true, global-core-realpath status=pass, remediation=null, and contract: global-core-realpath-pass. This violates plan.md:51, which promises that a disposable worktree package realpath warns, and permits a global command that breaks when the worktree is deleted to be certified healthy. Canonical-main discovery failure must remain unverifiable/non-pass, and the worktree path predicate must independently forbid the healthy marker; add a failed-topology-probe regression. severity: critical
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 makes failed canonical-main discovery in a Story worktree unverifiable/non-pass and independently forbids a disposable worktree package from receiving the healthy marker. The failed-topology regression and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs:109-119 claims to verify build-pipeline wiring by concatenating build-main-with-binding.mjs with promote-dist.mjs and searching for any chmod/bin text, while its ordering assertion inspects only promote-dist.mjs. It never asserts that build-main or build-utils imports/calls promoteDist and never executes either wrapper. A current-test temporary fixture kept the real promote-dist.mjs and a healthy executable live dist but replaced both build wrappers with `// deliberately unwired build wrapper`; with `RED_REPO_ROOT` bound to that fixture, the registered regression exited 0, printed `pipeline staging restore hook present: true`, emitted `contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored`, and printed the final GREEN summary. Thus CHK-001:happy:0 and CHK-002:happy:0 mechanical selectors can remain green after the actual build-to-promotion connection is removed; build-utils is not inspected at all. Add a structural assertion for both wrapper imports/calls or an end-to-end wrapper probe. This is distinct from F-041's Windows unreadable-shim branch and from the production defects F-037-F-042. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 3144360a65 makes the registered RED regression verify that both build wrappers import and call promoteDist, with mutation controls that replace each wrapper and prove the test bites. red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs and current full validation pass.

findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:0 lacks executable evidence for the second half of its must intent: appearing in proof-or-stop validation_plan output. The pinned command in checklist.json only parses proof-or-stop.config.json and prints the matching entry; it never invokes validation_plan, so planner discovery/output can regress while the selector remains green. A current `proof-or-stop validation_plan --storyId=B-e256 --tier=full --explain` run selected 132/132 commands, but the path packages/main/tests/red/red-global-cli-exec-bit.mjs appeared only as an unclassified material-path with `no impact index maps ... to a validation command`; the selected command unit is labeled only `configured validate.commands[84]`. The evidence note claims an unreceipted implementer transcript and therefore does not mechanically prove the promised planner output. This is distinct from F-043, which proves the red test false-passes when the build wrappers are unwired; this finding concerns validation-inventory/planner discoverability and its unsupported receipt. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commits 2fba3138c0 and 75dbee0167 preserve the immutable config-registration pin, add separate CHK-002:edge:1 planner discoverability intent, register stable red-global-cli-exec-bit id and label, and drive the production planCli renderer. Tool receipt 02846d4 has exit 0 and selectorMatched=true; current full validation passes 132/132.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:772-783 and packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:262-267: the F-037 repair still classifies a non-invoking Windows shim as healthy whenever a segment starts with node and merely contains the expected target anywhere. A current compiled-runtime probe used `node --version "<canonical dist/cli.js>"`; Node itself exited 0 and a marker proved the target script was not executed, while runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, no warnings, and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. The added regression covers an `echo` decoy only, not Node options such as `--version` (or `-e`) that consume the target as a non-script argument. This reopens the same Windows nonexecuting-reference false-pass family after F-037 was marked fixed and directly violates CHK-003 happy/adversarial and ProofStory AC-001. Validate the target executable argv position for accepted npm shim forms and add a mutation/regression proving option-consuming decoys cannot emit the marker. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit b480c94f5e validates the canonical Windows target only in Node's actual script argv position. Hermetic regressions prove node --version target and node -e source target do not execute the target and remain non-pass, while node -- target and representative npm shims pass. global-core-realpath.test.mjs, runtime fact contract, and current 132/132 full validation pass.

findings.desc: ProofStory acceptance topology omits a current must intent that its own acceptance claim promises. .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/proofstory.json:42-58 binds 15 verificationIntentRefs but omits CHK-001:edge:0, even though checklist.json declares that absent-bin-target behavior priority=must and AC-001 at proofstory.json:60 explicitly claims missing targets remain benign. packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts:2141-2174 derives REVIEW completeness only from effective binding verificationIntentRefs (plus milestones), so removing or staling CHK-001:edge:0 evidence would not produce review_completeness_missing_evidence. The current receipt passes, but the signed acceptance topology does not machine-bind this promised must behavior. Add CHK-001:edge:0 to AC-001 and refresh dependent acceptance artifacts. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: The PLAN-only proofstory_contract_set command updated AC-001 to bind CHK-001:edge:0 without dropping any prior reference. Independent scope check e521893 verified the set delta is exactly that one ref and all 16 must intents are bound. proofstory_review_completeness_check reports pass with zero gaps and current 132/132 full validation passes.

findings.desc: windows-shim-runtime-variable-binding false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:780-798 accepts the runtime tokens %_prog% and $_prog as Node solely by their spelling, without verifying what those variables are bound to. A current compiled-runtime probe used a canonical package, target, version, and PATH-selected .cmd shim containing SET "_prog=echo" followed by "%_prog%" "%~dp0\<canonical-relative-target>" %*. cmd.exe expands that invocation to echo the target rather than execute it, yet runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, warnings=[], and emitted contract: global-core-realpath-pass. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:178 only exercises the positive SET "_prog=node" form; the F-045 option-decoy mutations at lines 269-297 use a literal node token and cannot detect a malicious or broken variable binding. This is distinct from F-045 script-argv positioning: the target now occupies argv[0], but the supposed runtime is not Node. The current 132-command validation and focused suite remain green, so summary.json:3-5 and F-045 resolution prose overclaim that non-invoking Windows shims fail closed. Bind accepted runtime indirection to a verified Node assignment/control-flow form or reject unverified indirection, and add a mutation proving a non-Node _prog binding cannot emit the healthy marker. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 9473a6f32c removes trust in unbound Windows runtime variables and validates the official generated launcher grammar; the focused global-core fixture and the complete 132-command validation pass on the final material.

findings.desc: acceptance-basis-scope-binding-stale-after-repair: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/acceptance-basis.json:250,267 still signs scopeCheckDigest sha256:4e750b5b..., but the current verifier reports `AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING ... scope-check digest mismatch` after the later scope_check_save commit e521893d7f. The sequence is mechanically visible: e365326331 added CHK-001:edge:0 to AC-001 and generated the basis, then e521893d7f refreshed the independent scope check without regenerating that basis. Current `acceptance_topology_check` is therefore inconclusive with AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING even though `acceptance_rollout_report_read` and `acceptance_rollout_check` report PASS/current/full-3x2. F-046's semantic repair itself is correct—the only acceptance-binding semantic change is adding CHK-001:edge:0 and the acceptanceClaim is unchanged—but its verifier-owned topology evidence is not current to the final scope artifact. Regenerate/rebind the acceptance basis after the final scope check and refresh dependent pre-review/rollout evidence so the PASS chain cannot coexist with a scope-mismatched topology basis. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: The current acceptance-basis and independent scope-check were regenerated and re-attested after the repairs; pre_review_check reports plannedActual=complete and acceptance rollout reports a current full-3x2 receipt on the final Story binding.

findings.desc: windows-command-shim-unreachable-invocation false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:826-830 accepts a Windows command shim when any non-comment line contains a syntactically valid Node invocation of the canonical target, but it does not account for earlier unconditional control flow. A current compiled-runtime probe used a canonical package/target/version and a PATH-selected .cmd shim containing `goto :eof` before a literal `node <canonical-target> %*`; cmd.exe exits the batch file at `goto :eof`, so the target is unreachable, yet runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. The focused global-core-realpath suite remains green and contains no goto/exit/dead-branch mutation. This is distinct from F-047: the runtime token is literal Node and correctly positioned, but the invocation is dead code. Reject unreachable invocations or validate only a recognized executable npm-shim control-flow form, and add a regression proving an unconditional goto/exit or false short-circuit before the target cannot emit the healthy marker. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 9473a6f32c requires the validated Windows launcher invocation to be reachable in the supported execution grammar; unreachable accepted-looking lines are covered by the adversarial fixture and the final full validation passes.

findings.desc: windows-shim-target-base-variable-binding false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:772-778 strips both `%dp0%` and `$basedir` from the supposed script token without proving their cmd.exe meaning or binding. A current compiled-runtime probe against a canonical package/bin/version used literal `node` (so it is independent of F-047's `%_prog%` runtime issue) and three PATH-selected .cmd shims: an unbound `%dp0%`, `SET "dp0=C:\\definitely-wrong"` followed by `%dp0%`, and literal `$basedir`. All three returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`, although cmd.exe would expand the first two to an absent/wrong target and treats `$basedir` as literal text. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 covers only a `%~dp0` positive helper and has no mutation for invalid/unbound target-base forms. Bind `%dp0%` acceptance to the npm shim's verified `CALL :find_dp0`/`SET dp0=%~dp0` control flow, reject shell-inapplicable `$basedir` in a .cmd shim, and add mutations proving these target-base decoys cannot emit the healthy marker. This is a direct CHK-003/AC-001 Windows acceptance violation; severity: high.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 9473a6f32c validates the target base binding instead of stripping arbitrary %dp0% or $basedir text; target-base mutation coverage passes in the final focused and full validation.

findings.desc: acceptance-binding topology/proof absent independently of F-048: .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-e256/proofstory.json:34-62 defines high-assurance AC-001 and its 16 must intent refs but no `verificationTopology`. On the current frozen material, read-only `acceptance_topology_check --storyId=B-e256 --json` returns status=inconclusive, structuralPass=false, basisStatus=unsupported, topologyState=legacy_missing with AT_COVERAGE_BASIS_PARTIAL and AT_MISSING_TOPOLOGY in addition to F-048's separate AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING. The persisted plan basis is already `status: unsupported` at acceptance-basis.json:7, so merely rebinding its stale scope digest cannot establish topology. Independently, current `pre_review_check_read` returns status=inconclusive/ok=false with PR_COVERAGE_INCONCLUSIVE, PR_PRODUCTION_PATH_UNPROVEN, PR_MUTATION_EVIDENCE_MISSING, PR_MUTATION_DID_NOT_BITE, PR_CONTROL_NOT_RESTORED, PR_TRANSCRIPT_MISSING and PR_AUTHORITY_INADMISSIBLE; pre-review-check.json:437-446 persists that result against the current scope-check digest. This canonical lane requires executable verifier-owned topology/pre-review evidence, so AC-001 still lacks a passing structural and mutation-sensitive acceptance proof even after F-048 is repaired. Add the required verificationTopology and generate a current passing acceptance basis/pre-review proof with production-path, mutation/control-restoration and transcript evidence. Direct high-assurance acceptance/lifecycle evidence gap; severity: high.
findings.resolvedReason: Commits 9a8f26766f and 866a15937f bind pre-review and production proof scenarios to the active Story; the 58-assertion terminal contract, pre_review_check, acceptance-basis smoke, and full validation all pass on the final binding.

findings.desc: windows-command-shim-posix-single-quote false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:765-769 tokenizes both double-quoted and single-quoted strings, then lines 780-798 use those tokens to certify a PATH-selected Windows .cmd shim. cmd.exe does not treat single quotes as quoting. Current compiled-runtime probes using a canonical package/target/version returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass` for both `'node' "<canonical-target>" %*` and `node '<canonical-target>' %*`; on cmd.exe the first command name includes apostrophes and is not the standard Node runtime, while the second passes apostrophes as literal target characters rather than invoking the canonical file. The focused global-core-realpath suite remains green and contains no single-quote shim mutation. This is distinct from F-047 runtime-variable binding, F-049 unreachable control flow, and F-050 target-base-variable binding: it is cross-shell tokenization/quoting semantics. Parse .cmd using cmd.exe quoting rules or reject single-quoted runtime/target tokens, and add both negative mutations so neither can emit the healthy marker. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 9473a6f32c accepts only the supported Windows command quoting grammar and rejects POSIX single-quote lookalikes; the corresponding mutation and final full validation pass.

findings.desc: windows-command-shim-caret-escaped-separator false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:746-758 splits every unquoted `&`/`|` into executable command segments without honoring cmd.exe caret escaping, and lines 826-830 accept any later segment that looks like a Node invocation. A current compiled-runtime probe used the canonical installed package/bin/version and a PATH-selected .cmd shim containing `echo ^& node "<canonical-target>" %*`. In cmd.exe, `^&` is a literal ampersand passed to echo, so the `node ...` text is not a separate command and the target is never executed; nevertheless runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 and 249-297 cover a representative shim, echo decoy, and Node option decoys, but no escaped-command-separator mutation. This is distinct from F-047 runtime-variable binding, F-049 unreachable control flow, F-050 target-base binding, and F-052 single-quote tokenization: the runtime and target tokens are literal and correctly positioned, but the parser invents a command boundary that cmd.exe explicitly escapes. Parse cmd.exe caret escapes or accept only a verified npm-generated shim grammar, and add a mutation proving an escaped separator cannot emit the healthy marker. severity: high
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 9473a6f32c handles cmd caret escaping without treating escaped separators as valid executable boundaries; adversarial mutation coverage and final full validation pass.

findings.desc: official npm PowerShell shim is outside the validated command-selection contract: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1795-1826 resolves a Windows `proof-or-stop` only through PATHEXT candidates (default .COM/.EXE/.BAT/.CMD), while npm's locally installed official cmd-shim@8.0.0 generator creates three peer entrypoints: extensionless shell, `.cmd`, and `.ps1`. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 supplies only a hand-written `.cmd` positive that is not the official control-flow shape, and repository search finds no `.ps1` fixture. A current compiled-runtime probe generated the official shims, changed only `proof-or-stop.ps1` to invoke `other-package/dist/cli.js`, left the official `.cmd` healthy, and used the production Windows resolver with PATH pointing at that prefix and PATHEXT=.CMD;.EXE. It selected `proof-or-stop.CMD`, returned global-core-realpath status=pass/verification=ok, and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`; the PowerShell entrypoint was never inspected. This is distinct from F-047/F-049/F-050/F-052, which validate syntax/data flow inside a selected `.cmd`: this family is failure to bind the shell-selected official npm entrypoint at all. Add exact positive fixtures generated by the supported npm cmd-shim for both `.cmd` and `.ps1`, model PowerShell selection or inspect all applicable peer shims, and add inverse mutations showing a mismatched/missing/unreadable `.ps1` cannot be hidden by a healthy `.cmd` when PowerShell is the invocation surface. Direct CHK-003/AC-001 Windows compatibility and acceptance-proof gap; severity: high.
findings.resolvedReason: Commit 9473a6f32c verifies the official npm Windows command and PowerShell peer launcher contracts; simulated Windows peer coverage and final full validation pass.

findings.desc: windows-command-shim-argument-forwarding false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:780-798 proves only that Node receives the canonical target in script position; it never requires the selected Windows .cmd shim to forward caller arguments with `%*`. A current compiled-runtime probe used a canonical package/target/version and a PATH-selected shim containing only `node "<lexical canonical target>"` (no `%*`); runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. Under cmd.exe that shim executes the target but discards `--version`, so it cannot deliver checklist.json CHK-001.userSees (`proof-or-stop --version prints the compiled version`) or the claimed working global command contract. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 includes `%*` only in the positive helper and has no missing-forwarding mutation. This is distinct from F-047 runtime binding, F-049 reachability, F-050 target-base binding, and F-052 quoting: runtime and target are literal, reachable, correctly quoted, and correctly normalized; only argv propagation is absent. Require the recognized cmd npm shim invocation to forward `%*` (and define any separately supported PowerShell `$args` shape rather than conflating shell grammars), then add a negative mutation proving a no-forwarding shim cannot emit the healthy marker. severity: high

windows-command-shim-exit-status-not-preserved false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:826-833 certifies a Windows shim from the existence of any accepted target invocation and never verifies what the batch file returns after that invocation. A current compiled-runtime probe used the canonical installed package/bin/version and a PATH-selected .cmd shim `node "<canonical-target>" %*` followed by `exit /b 0`; runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. Under cmd.exe the target is reachable and receives its arguments, but the final `exit /b 0` masks every nonzero Proof-or-Stop exit, so automation can treat rejected/failed commands as success. This violates checklist.json:10,25's working npm-shim compatibility contract. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 checks only a positive representative shim and has no mutation for post-invocation status masking. This is distinct from F-049 (target unreachable) and F-055 (arguments discarded): here the target executes with `%*`, but its result is discarded. Require a recognized npm-generated control-flow/exit-propagation shape or execute a bounded semantic probe, and add a failing-command mutation proving the selected shim preserves the target exit status. severity: high

windows-non-batch-PATHEXT-entrypoint parsed as cmd shim false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:801-833 sends every Windows PATH-selected entrypoint to validateWindowsCommandShim as UTF-8 batch text, while lines 1811-1831 deliberately select all PATHEXT candidates including the default .COM and .EXE before .BAT/.CMD. A current compiled-runtime probe supplied an otherwise canonical package, target, and compiled version plus a PATH-selected plain-text proof-or-stop.exe containing `node "<canonical-target>" %*`; Windows cannot execute that file as a PE/COM program or batch shim, yet runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, warnings=[], and emitted contract: global-core-realpath-pass. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:229-355 covers .cmd and PATHEXT ordering but has no selected .COM/.EXE format/launchability mutation. This is distinct from F-054, which leaves an official .ps1 peer uninspected, and F-047/F-049/F-050/F-052/F-053/F-055, which concern semantics inside a selected batch shim: here the selected artifact is not a batch language artifact at all. Fail closed for non-.bat/.cmd PATHEXT entries unless their native executable contract is independently verified, and add a mutation proving an invalid/textual .exe or .com cannot emit the healthy marker. Direct CHK-003 happy:0/adversarial:2 and AC-001 acceptance violation; severity: high

windows-command-shim-argument-injection false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:780-798 validates only the runtime token and canonical target in Node script position; it does not constrain argv after that target. A current compiled-runtime probe supplied an otherwise canonical package/version/PATH-selected .cmd containing `node "<canonical-target>" definitely-no-such-command %*`; runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and rendered the healthy row. Yet the concrete CLI witness `node packages/main/dist/cli.js definitely-no-such-command --version` exits 1 with `Unknown command`, whereas the caller-intended `node packages/main/dist/cli.js --version` exits 0 and prints the version. Thus a shim may forward `%*` and execute the right target but still prepend an argument that replaces/corrupts the caller operation, while doctor certifies it healthy. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:229-355 has Node-option decoys and one positive npm-shaped shim but no extra-argv mutation. This is distinct from F-055 missing forwarding: requiring `%*` does not reject this witness; it is also distinct from F-056 because exit propagation may be exact. Require the supported npm-generated invocation tail to preserve caller argv without injected prefix/suffix arguments (or execute a bounded semantic probe), and add a mutation proving extra arguments cannot emit the healthy marker. Direct CHK-001 userSees and CHK-003 happy:0/adversarial:2 acceptance violation; severity: high

windows-command-shim-output-redirection false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:780-833 verifies only that some parsed segment invokes Node with the canonical target; it ignores redirection attached to that invocation. A current compiled-runtime probe used an otherwise canonical installed package/version and PATH-selected .cmd shim `node "%~dp0\\node_modules\\@proof-or-stop\\core\\dist\\cli.js" %* >NUL`; runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. Under cmd.exe the target is reachable, caller argv is forwarded exactly, and its exit status is preserved, but `>NUL` suppresses the `proof-or-stop --version` stdout that CHK-001.userSees explicitly promises. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 has only a positive representative shim and no target-invocation stdout/stderr redirection mutation. This is distinct from F-049 reachability, F-055 missing forwarding, F-058 argv injection, and F-056 exit-status masking: execution, argv, and status can all be correct while the required observable output is discarded. Validate a recognized official npm target-invocation tail without output redirection or execute a bounded semantic `--version` witness that asserts stdout, and add `>NUL`/`2>NUL` inverse fixtures without rejecting npm's unrelated `goto ... 2>NUL` control segment. Direct Story acceptance violation; severity: high.

canonical-command-name absence masked by legacy lattice fallback: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:1792-1808 defines resolveCliCommandPath as `resolveCommandOnPath("proof-or-stop") ?? resolveCommandOnPath("lattice")`, so the doctor may certify a legacy lattice executable when the user-facing proof-or-stop command is entirely absent. A current compiled-runtime production-resolver probe created an otherwise canonical global package/bin/version, no proof-or-stop PATH artifact, and only a valid lattice.cmd pointing at the canonical target; with win32/PATHEXT=.CMD the check selected lattice.CMD, returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. This directly contradicts plan.md CHK-003 (`A global package without a proof-or-stop command on PATH is non-pass`), checklist CHK-001 userSees (`proof-or-stop --version` works), and CHK-003 edge:1. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:377-402 covers null PATH resolution but has no legacy-only lattice sibling mutation. It is distinct from F-047–F-058: the selected legacy shim can be an exact, reachable, argument-preserving, status-preserving official npm shape; the defect is that the canonical command name being promised is absent. Remove the lattice fallback from this canonical health fact or report it as non-pass compatibility-only evidence, and add POSIX/Windows legacy-only PATH mutations. Direct operator-visible acceptance violation; severity: high

windows-command-shim-node-runtime-unavailable false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:780-798 accepts literal `node`, `%_prog%`, or `$_prog` from text and lines 801-833 sets executable=true without resolving or launching the runtime selected by the shim. The locally installed npm cmd-shim generator (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/cmd-shim/lib/index.js:98-118) uses its official branch to select adjacent `%dp0%\\node.exe` when present and otherwise `_prog=node`, so a correct binding is not proof that Node is launchable. A current compiled-runtime probe used that official GOTO/find_dp0/IF EXIST/SETLOCAL invocation shape, a canonical package/bin/compiled version, production Windows PATH/PATHEXT selection, PATH containing only the shim directory, no adjacent node.exe and no node/node.cmd/node.exe artifact anywhere on the modeled PATH. `runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks` nevertheless selected proof-or-stop.CMD, returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`; actual cmd.exe execution would fail before the canonical target starts because `_prog=node` cannot resolve. packages/main/tests/global-core-realpath.test.mjs:175-179 covers the positive representative shim but has no missing-selected-runtime mutation. This is distinct from F-047: `_prog` is correctly bound to Node here rather than rebound to echo; and distinct from F-049/F-055/F-056/F-058/F-059 because reachability, target/argv/status/output syntax are otherwise official while the runtime executable itself is absent. Verify the selected official runtime branch is launchable or execute a bounded semantic `proof-or-stop --version` witness, and add adjacent-node-absent plus PATH-node-absent inverse coverage. Direct CHK-001 user-visible and CHK-003 happy:0 host-executable-contract violation; severity: high.

windows-command-shim-adjacent-quoted-token-concatenation false pass: packages/main/src/core/runtime-environment-checks.ts:762-769 tokenizes a double-quoted fragment and immediately adjacent unquoted characters as separate tokens, then lines 780-798 certifies the quoted canonical target as the first Node script argument while ignoring the adjacent suffix. A current compiled-runtime probe used an otherwise canonical package, bin target, compiled version, and PATH-selected .cmd shim `node "%~dp0\\node_modules\\@proof-or-stop\\core\\dist\\cli.js"garbage %*`; runRuntimeEnvironmentChecks returned global-core-realpath status=pass, verification=ok, executable=true, warnings=[], and emitted `contract: global-core-realpath-pass`. Under cmd.exe, adjacent quoted and unquoted fragments form one argv token, so Node receives a nonexistent `cli.jsgarbage` script rather than the canonical target and the global command fails before Proof-or-Stop starts. The focused fixture has no adjacent-fragment mutation. This is distinct from F-052, where single quotes are misinterpreted as quoting; F-058, where a separate fixed argv is inserted after a valid target; F-059 redirection; and F-061 runtime unavailability. Parse cmd.exe token concatenation correctly or accept only the exact supported npm-generated invocation grammar, and add mutations for quoted-target suffix and prefix adjacency so neither can emit the healthy marker. Direct CHK-001 user-visible and CHK-003 happy:0/adversarial:2 acceptance violation; severity: high.
